chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed two rak'ahs then stood up. He said, 'He faces [the Qibla].' I said, 'What do the people narrate?' So he mentioned to him the hadith of Dhil-Shimalayn, and he said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not leave his place, and if he had left, he would have faced [the Qibla].'

key_terms.حَدِيثَ ذِي اَلشِّمَالَيْنِ: the hadith of Dhil-Shimalayn (referring to the Prophet facing the Qibla with both shoulders)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they stand up from prayer after two rak'ahs due to forgetfulness?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedure for a worshipper who stands up due to forgetfulness, confirming they should face the Qibla. The Imam reinforces this by citing the Prophet’s practice of remaining in his place rather than turning around, establishing the principle of stability and continuity during the transition. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the integrity of prayer even when errors occur, distinguishing it from other schools that may require different corrective actions.
